text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Christopher de Souza –   23 To ask the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (a) what caused the flash floods in and surrounding the Bukit Timah-Dunearn Canal and Ulu Pandan Canal on 17 April 2021; (b) whether the overflow of water from the canals onto the roads and the park connectors, respectively, can be prevented; and (c) what engineering measures will be put in place to mitigate against such overflows in the future such as to make the areas safe for residents, pedestrians and motorists during heavy downpours.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This rainfall resulted in flash floods occurring at Bukit Timah and Dunearn Roads near Sime Darby Centre and a stretch of the Park Connectors along Ulu Pandan Canal.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is a map of the stretch of roads that I mentioned in my reply.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Just a bit of landmark, Sime Darby Centre is the block marked in black.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB Quick Response Teams were on site directing traffic and assisting affected residents by issuing inflatable flood bags and portable flood barriers to prevent floodwaters from entering their homes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members who have been on the Rail Corridor hike would not miss this impressive infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is somewhere after you have crossed Bukit Timah Railway Station and another 500 metres or so, you will come to this stretch, which opens up to the area at Old Holland Road.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, it is impressive because it is large and deep.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And I think it has helped significantly on this day of 17 April, because the flood on this day is nowhere near the earlier floods that we had seen along the same stretch of roads when lesser rain fell.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Water level sensors on this stretch – the sensor is placed where the yellow triangle is located – installed along the upgraded stretch of Bukit Timah Canal from Jalan Kampong Chantek to Sixth Avenue, just upstream of the expanded Bukit Timah First Diversion Canal, showed the section of the canal was 50% full, 50% full, on 17 April with no flash floods along that stretch despite the heavy rainfall.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When completed, we expect the top water level in this section of the Canal to be lower by over one metre for the same rainfall intensity experienced on 17 April.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Another stretch, which is along Ulu Pandan Canal, a low-lying 300-metre stretch – as marked in red – of the Park Connector next to the Ulu Pandan Canal was also flooded on 17 April even though major roads – the major roads are Clementi Road in grey, Clementi Avenue 6, Commonwealth Avenue West and the Ayer Rajah Expressway – served by the Canal did not experience flooding.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB will raise this low-lying section of the Park Connector when PUB reconstructs the Ulu Pandan Canal in tandem with future developments.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Drainage design standards were also raised in 2011 to cater for higher intensity rainfall, as part of PUB's broader efforts to address the impact of climate change.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is, however, not practical to expand our drains to accommodate every extreme rainfall event as this would require massive land take and much higher costs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB will put in place cost-effective measures to minimise flood risks and better manage flood events.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For instance, PUB is currently upgrading its rainfall forecasting radar technology, which will help improve prediction of locations where heavy rainfall might occur and enhance response time to potential flash floods.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB also works closely with LTA and Traffic Police during heavy storms to monitor road conditions and notify motorists of flooded roads to avoid through electronic road signages, online and social media platforms and radio broadcasts.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Members of the public can be alerted on flash floods by subscribing to the National Environment Agency's and PUB's weather forecast and water level SMS alerts or access the mobile app, "myENV", for updates on impending heavy rain and the water level in drains at designated locations.
